sections.vendors: Tesco F&F works with supply chain partners across Bangladesh, India, China, and Turkey. The brand is increasing supply chain transparency with a stepped-up effort to disclose second-tier (fabric/processing) suppliers. Tesco published its Progress Sustainability Report 2026 covering key supply chain metrics.
sections.sustainability: Tesco F&F continues its Detox chemical management programme, aligning with ZDHC Foundation standards for wet processing suppliers. The brand is targeting 100% more sustainable cotton sourcing (achieved for most lines by 2025) and 100% responsibly sourced fabrics by 2030.
sections.sourcing: Tesco is working collaboratively with supplier partners to create 'planet plans' — ESG roadmaps aligned with Tesco's own sustainability targets. This top-down ESG alignment strategy means F&F suppliers need to demonstrate credible decarbonisation and water management plans.
sections.strategy: F&F continues to perform as a key clothing destination within Tesco's superstore estate. The brand leverages Tesco's Clubcard data for personalised clothing promotions. Tesco's broader sustainability report 2026 shows clothing as a key focus area for circular economy initiatives.
sections.pricing: F&F competes in the supermarket clothing segment alongside George and TU. Pricing remains anchored at everyday value levels, with seasonal promotional events driving volume. No significant pricing shifts signalled.
sections.launches: F&F launched AW2026 ranges with expanded sustainable materials content, including organic cotton childrenswear and recycled polyester outerwear. The brand's school uniform range maintained its market-leading position in the supermarket segment.
sections.gossip: Tesco's move to ask suppliers to co-develop 'planet plans' is seen as an ambitious but resource-intensive approach. Smaller suppliers without dedicated ESG teams may struggle to produce the level of reporting Tesco is requesting, creating a potential tier-of-supply bifurcation.
soWhat: Tesco's supplier 'planet plan' requirement means F&F suppliers need formalised ESG documentation — suppliers without scope 1/2 emissions data and a decarbonisation plan should develop one urgently
ZDHC chemical management alignment means all wet processors supplying F&F must work towards ZDHC Gateway compliance — this is now a threshold requirement, not a nice-to-have
100% responsible fabrics by 2030 target gives a 4-year runway — suppliers should develop a certified fibre roadmap now and present it proactively to Tesco buyers as a partnership asset
